| [MATH: x] | [MATH: -8] | [MATH: -1] | [MATH: 0] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 8] |

Notice that we included both positive and negative input values since the cube root is defined over all real numbers.

- Its range is [MATH: y \in (-\infty,\infty).]
- The function is increasing throughout its entire domain.
- As [MATH: x \rightarrow \infty,] we have [MATH: y\rightarrow \infty,] though the function increases more slowly as [MATH: x] gets large.
- As [MATH: x \rightarrow -\infty,] we have [MATH: y\rightarrow -\infty,] though the function decreases more slowly as [MATH: x] becomes very negative.

sections.normalized_html:
Let's start by recalling the graph of [MATH: y=\sqrt[3]{x}.]

Now, let's examine each statement in turn.

  • Statement I is true. Indeed, [MATH: f(64)=\sqrt[3]{64}=4.]

  • Statement II is false since [MATH: f(x) =\sqrt[3]{x}] is defined for [MATH: x \in (-\infty, \infty).]

  • Statement III is true. Indeed, [MATH: f(x) \rightarrow -\infty] as [MATH: x \rightarrow -\infty.]

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
